name: The Landscape of Agentic Reinforcement Learning for LLMs: A Survey
venue: arXiv:2509.02547 (submitted 2 Sep 2025, v5 17 Apr 2026); accepted to / published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), OpenReview forum RY19y2RI1O.
authors_affiliation: Guibin Zhang, Hejia Geng, Xiaohang Yu (equal contribution) ... Zhenfei Yin, Lei Bai (corresponding); 25 authors total. Primary affiliations: University of Oxford; Shanghai AI Laboratory; National University of Singapore; UIUC; Brown University; University College London; USTC; Imperial College London; Dalian University of Technology; Chinese Academy of Sciences; CUHK; University of Georgia; UC San Diego; UC Santa Barbara; University of Bristol.
code_url: N/A (survey; no method code). Companion OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=RY19y2RI1O
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/xhyumiracle/Awesome-AgenticLLM-RL-Papers (official maintained paper list, ~1.8k stars / 79 forks, actively updated)
task_domain: Survey of agentic reinforcement learning (Agentic RL) for LLMs. Spans a twofold taxonomy: (a) core agentic capabilities (planning, tool use, memory, reasoning, self-improvement, perception), and (b) task domains: search/research agents, code agents, mathematical agents, GUI agents, vision agents, embodied agents, and multi-agent systems. Retrieval/tool-use/memory are treated as RL-controlled agentic capabilities rather than static modules.
problem_setting: Survey synthesizing 500+ works. Formalizes the conceptual shift from PBRFT/LLM-RL (modeled as a degenerate single-step MDP over a prompt -> response) to Agentic RL, which is cast as a temporally extended, partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) with multi-step interaction, environment state, action space (text actions + structured agentic actions such as tool calls), stochastic transition dynamics, and (often sparse / verifiable) rewards. Settings covered are interactive and long-horizon, single- and multi-agent, with supervision ranging from verifiable outcome rewards (RLVR) to preference/process rewards. The central thesis: RL is the mechanism that turns heuristic static capability modules (planning, tool use, memory, reasoning) into adaptive, robust agentic behavior.
what_is_retrieved: As a survey it reviews what RL-controlled agentic memory/tool subsystems store and retrieve: external documents/web pages (RAG-style search agents), tools/APIs, episodic memory entries, natural-language memory tokens (explicit) and latent memory tokens (implicit), structured/graph memory (temporal KG), skills, and prior experiences/trajectories. Retrieval is framed as an RL-learnable decision (what to store, when to retrieve, how to forget).
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID across the surveyed field. Covers retrieval over STATIC external corpora/web/tools (RL-based search agents like Search-R1, R1-Searcher; tool retrieval) AND over GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes and manages with an RL policy (MemAgent, MEM1, ReSum, MemoryLLM/M+, MemGen, structured/graph memory). The RAG-style-vs-token-level-vs-structured memory taxonomy directly spans the static-corpus vs growing-memory distinction.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Not a primary survey axis. The optimizing objective discussed is the RL learning objective (maximize expected/cumulative reward of the agent's trajectory), not a fixed top-k retrieval ranking or completeness-of-minimal-set metric. Retrieval quality is generally subsumed into downstream task reward rather than analyzed as a top-k vs completeness tradeoff. [uncertain] as a unifying axis.
retrieval_unit: Reviewed across granularities (survey): document/web page (search agents), tool/API call, natural-language memory token/segment (explicit memory), latent memory token/embedding (implicit memory), knowledge-graph node/subgraph (structured memory), full trajectory/experience, and skill. No single canonical unit.
index_source: Survey covers all: static external corpora/web/tool sets (RAG-style search agents, TIR tool stores) and online/test-time growing memory written and pruned by the agent during interaction (MemAgent natural-language memory pool, MEM1, ReSum context summarization, MemoryLLM/M+ self-updatable latent memory). Hybrid is the dominant picture; the memory chapter explicitly traces evolution from RAG-style external memory to trainable token-level and structured memory.
index_structure_topology: Survey reviews flat external corpora/vector stores (RAG-style), natural-language memory pools, fixed-size latent memory-token banks (MemoryLLM/M+), and structured/graph memory (temporal knowledge graph in Zep; structured memory as a 'prospective' direction). No single topology; structured/graph memory is highlighted as an emerging trend.
retriever_type: Survey-level: covers off-the-shelf dense retrieval over external corpora (search agents), generative/agent-issued retrieval where the LLM emits search/tool calls, and RL-controlled memory controllers that decide retrieval/retention. Emphasis is on retrieval/memory access becoming an RL-learned decision rather than a fixed retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: Central surveyed shift: from off-the-shelf similarity retrieval toward RL-optimized retrieval/memory-management policies trained with outcome/verifiable rewards (RLVR). Search agents (Search-R1, R1-Searcher, ZeroSearch, ReSearch) learn when/what to retrieve via RL on final-answer reward; memory agents (MemAgent, MEM1, ReSum) train an RL policy controlling what to store/retrieve/overwrite. Also covers SFT/imitation and process/preference signals as alternatives.
query_construction: Not unified (survey). Reviews agent-issued queries: the LLM generates explicit search/tool-call queries interleaved with reasoning (TIR), reasoning-conditioned queries, and learned memory-trigger decisions. Query construction is itself part of the RL-trained policy in agentic search.
query_granularity: Survey spans task-level (one-shot retrieval), trajectory-level, and step/turn-level retrieval. The multi-turn TIR and RAG-style memory discussions emphasize per-step/per-turn retrieval decisions interleaved across a long-horizon rollout.
when_to_retrieve: Survey-level: covers one-shot, iterative, and adaptive/learned (agent-initiated) retrieval. A core theme is that Agentic RL lets the agent autonomously learn WHEN to retrieve / invoke tools / access memory, moving from fixed schedules to RL-learned, agent-initiated retrieval decisions.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Survey reviews fixed schedules, model/agent-initiated requests (the policy emits a retrieve/tool/memory token), and RL-learned triggers (memory controllers deciding per-segment what to retain/overwrite, e.g. MemAgent; learned memory triggers, e.g. MemGen). The WHEN-to-retrieve decision is framed as part of the learned agentic policy rather than a single hand-set signal.
reranking: Not a focal survey axis; reranking of retrieved context is not analyzed as a standalone dimension. [uncertain]
retrieved_context_refinement: Survey covers post-retrieval / context-management refinement, especially context compression and summarization for long-horizon memory: ReSum (context summarization), context folding, MemAgent (compress long context into concise natural-language summaries), and MEM1 (synergize memory and reasoning). Refinement is framed as RL-controlled what-to-retain/overwrite/compress rather than classic rerank-then-distill.
how_retrieved_used: Survey-level: prompt/context augmentation (RAG-style search agents inject retrieved docs), tool-integrated reasoning (retrieved tool outputs woven into the reasoning loop), memory injection (natural-language or latent memory tokens fed into the forward pass), skill reuse, and as RL training signal (outcome reward shapes when/how retrieval is used). Latent-token injection (MemoryLLM/M+, MemGen) is explicitly covered.
planning_integration: Survey distinguishes two RL-planning paradigms: (i) RL as an EXTERNAL GUIDE to a structured planning/search process (e.g. RL-scored nodes inside tree/MCTS-style planning), and (ii) RL as an INTERNAL DRIVER that directly evolves the LLM's intrinsic planning policy via outcome reward. Retrieval/tool use is interleaved per-step within these planning loops (TIR), and plan-then-act / retrieve-then-reason patterns are reviewed.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Survey emphasizes deep interleaving: from post-hoc ReAct-style tool calling to Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR) that embeds tool/retrieval calls within the cognitive/reasoning loop, up to multi-turn TIR with temporal credit assignment. Granularity spans per-CoT-step and per-tool-call within a rollout (interleaved reasoning + acting).
retrieved_item_representation: Survey covers raw retrieved documents/tool outputs, distilled/summarized context (ReSum, MemAgent summaries), explicit human-readable natural-language memory tokens, latent/soft memory tokens (MemoryLLM/M+, MemGen, IMM), and structured/graph memory (temporal KG). Spans surface text to machine-native latent representations.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Survey spans the spectrum: raw retrieved documents/trajectories, compressed/summarized context, distilled experiential/latent memory (MemGen generative latent memory carrying experiential knowledge), and structured graph memory. Notes the move from flat token memory toward more abstract structured/latent representations.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Survey discusses robustness implicitly via RL outcome optimization (agents learn to recover from tool/retrieval errors rather than mimic static patterns), context compression to reduce distractors (ReSum, MemAgent), and verifiable-reward training. Trustworthiness (Sec 6.1) flags hallucination/reward-hacking risks but a single noise-robustness retrieval taxonomy is not formalized. [uncertain]
memory_type: Survey memory taxonomy (Table 3) organizes agent memory into three classic categories with RL-marked variants: (1) RAG-style / external memory, (2) token-level memory (explicit natural-language tokens, e.g. MemAgent/MEM1/Memory Token; and implicit latent tokens, e.g. MemoryLLM/M+/IMM/MemGen), and (3) (prospective) structured memory (temporal knowledge graph, e.g. Zep). So: episodic + latent + graph + RAG-style.
write_back: Yes (central theme of the memory chapter). The survey frames RL-controlled memory as deciding what to store, when to retrieve, and how to forget; memory controllers write/overwrite natural-language or latent memory during interaction (MemAgent retain/overwrite per segment; MemoryLLM/M+ self-updatable latent memory; MemGen generating experiential memory).
online_growth: Yes. Token-level and RAG-style memory grow/update during deployment: MemAgent maintains and updates a natural-language memory pool per segment; ReSum/context-folding compress accumulating context online; MemoryLLM/M+ are self-updatable at test time. Online growth/management of memory is a first-class surveyed dimension (vs frozen offline stores).
write_back_trigger: Survey covers RL-learned/per-segment writes (MemAgent decides per segment which tokens to retain/overwrite), summarization-triggered writes (ReSum, context folding), and continual latent updates (MemoryLLM/M+ update memory tokens as context evolves). No single trigger; writes are increasingly RL-policy-decided rather than fixed.
failure_experience_usage: Survey notes RL agents learn from both successful and failed trajectories (e.g. self-improvement / reflection methods and outcome-reward training that penalizes failures), but a dedicated success-vs-failure memory-storage taxonomy is not a focal axis for the memory chapter. [uncertain]
memory_evolution_update: Survey reviews post-write dynamics: overwrite/retain decisions (MemAgent), compression/summarization-based consolidation (ReSum, context folding), continual update of fixed latent memory tokens (MemoryLLM/M+ repeatedly retrieved, integrated, and updated, with strong resistance to forgetting), and prospective structured/graph memory evolution (temporal KG). Update is framed as RL-controlled retain/overwrite/compress.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes (a defining surveyed theme). The survey's thesis is precisely that retrieval/tool/memory access becomes an RL-learned policy: search agents learn when/what to retrieve via RL (Search-R1, R1-Searcher), and memory controllers are RL policies deciding store/retrieve/forget (MemAgent, MEM1). Marked with daggers in Table 3 for works directly employing RL.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes (surveyed). Section 4.7 covers Multi-Agent Systems and RL for multi-agent collaboration, and MARTI is reviewed as a framework for reinforced training/inference of multi-agent LLM systems. Shared/collective experience across agents is discussed as part of the multi-agent and self-improvement directions.
benchmarks: Consolidated compendium (Table 10) of environments/benchmarks by capability and domain: Web (WebShop, Mind2Web/Mind2Web 2, WebArena, VisualWebArena, AppWorld); GUI (AndroidWorld, OSWorld, MiniWoB++); Coding/SWE (SWE-bench, Debug-Gym, and interactive SWE environments); Math; Search/Research (search-agent benchmarks); Embodied (ALFWorld/ScienceWorld-style, Minecraft); Tool (tool-use benchmarks); Multi-agent. Plus a frameworks table (Table 11).
benchmark_family: Spans web (Mind2Web/WebArena/WebShop/AppWorld/VisualWebArena), GUI/computer-use (OSWorld/AndroidWorld/MiniWoB++), code/SWE (SWE-bench/Debug-Gym), math, search/deep-research, embodied (Minecraft/ALFWorld-style), tool-use, and multi-agent. Organized by agent capability (Reasoning/Planning/Tool Use/Memory/Collaboration/Self-Improve) x task domain x modality.
baselines: N/A as a survey (no head-to-head method baselines). It contrasts itself conceptually with prior LLM-RL / agent surveys (e.g. 'A Survey of Frontiers in LLM Reasoning' Ke et al. 2025; LLM/VLM-integrated RL surveys) and positions Agentic RL against PBRFT/conventional LLM-RL.
key_metrics: N/A as a survey (no single empirical metric). Discusses RL learning objectives and reward functions (verifiable/outcome rewards, process rewards, preference rewards) and capability/task success as the relevant evaluation signals; tabulates environments by capability rather than reporting numbers.
headline_result: N/A (survey, no empirical headline number). Headline contribution: a formalization of Agentic RL as a POMDP (vs degenerate single-step MDP of LLM-RL) and a comprehensive twofold taxonomy (six agentic capabilities x task domains), synthesizing 500+ works, plus a consolidated compendium of open-source environments (Table 10) and RL frameworks (Table 11).
ablations: N/A (survey; no controlled ablations). Provides structured comparison tables instead: RL-algorithm variant comparison (Table 2: REINFORCE/PPO/GRPO/DPO families), agent-memory categories (Table 3, RL-marked), environments/benchmarks (Table 10), and RL frameworks (Table 11).
evaluation_decoupling: Survey implicitly advocates capability-decoupled evaluation: environments/benchmarks are catalogued by which agentic capability they probe (Reasoning/Planning/Tool Use/Memory/Collaboration/Self-Improve), separating component capability evaluation from end-to-end task success. Intrinsic retrieval metrics vs end-task metrics are not separated as a dedicated axis. [uncertain]
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Survey discusses both outcome rewards (RLVR / verifiable final-answer rewards) and process/intermediate signals (process reward models, step-wise / temporal credit assignment for multi-turn TIR), noting the challenge of credit assignment over long horizons as a key open problem.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Survey discusses efficiency at the training-systems level (Sec 5.2 / Sec 6.2): asynchronous/distributed RL frameworks and rollout/experience-generation bottlenecks (e.g. AWorld reports a 14.6x speedup over single-node execution by parallelizing rollouts). Memory works target context-length/efficiency (ReSum, MemAgent compress long context). Not a single cost-vs-accuracy curve.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Discussed qualitatively via long-context/memory management (compressing long inputs into concise summaries, fixed-size latent memory-token banks in MemoryLLM/M+, segment-wise retain/overwrite in MemAgent) rather than a prescribed top-k or token budget. [uncertain] as a concrete recipe.
survey_scope_and_axes: Explicit organizing axes: (1) Preliminary formalization LLM-RL (single-step MDP) vs Agentic RL (POMDP), covering environment state, action space, transition dynamics, reward, learning objective, and RL algorithms (REINFORCE/PPO/GRPO/DPO). (2) Capability perspective: Planning, Tool Use, Memory, Self-Improvement, Reasoning, Perception, Others. (3) Task perspective: Search/Research, Code, Math, GUI, Vision, Embodied, Multi-Agent, Others. (4) Environments & Frameworks compendium (Table 10 environments, Table 11 frameworks). (5) Open challenges (trustworthiness, scaling training, scaling environments, mechanistic debate, deployment, social impact). Synthesizes 500+ works; coverage window through 2025 (v5 revised Apr 2026).
builds_on: Builds on and organizes LLM-RL / RLHF foundations (PPO, GRPO, DPO, REINFORCE, RLVR a la DeepSeek-R1) and agentic methods it taxonomizes (ReAct, Toolformer, Search-R1/R1-Searcher, MemAgent/MEM1/ReSum, MemoryLLM/M+, MemGen, Reflexion-style self-improvement, Voyager-style skills). Relates to prior surveys on LLM reasoning and LLM/VLM-integrated RL.
contrasts_with: Explicitly contrasts Agentic RL with conventional LLM-RL / Preference-Based RL Fine-Tuning (PBRFT), framed as a degenerate single-step MDP, and with prompt-engineering/SFT-only agent pipelines (static, imitation-based) that lack adaptation through experience. Also positioned relative to other recent surveys (LLM reasoning; LLM/VLM-integrated RL; agentic systems).
lineage: Surveys lineage. A foundational taxonomy/compendium survey for the Agentic-RL line, organizing RL-trained agentic capabilities (planning, tool use, memory, reasoning, self-improvement, perception). Relevant to the retrieval-as-learned-policy and write-back/online-growth axes that separate RL-controlled experience/memory agents from static RAG planners.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (survey, not a CBR method). Does not implement a Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle; experience reuse appears via RL self-improvement and memory rather than explicit CBR.
explicit_cbr_grounding: No. The survey does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not center Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; experience reuse is framed through RL, memory, and self-improvement rather than the CBR ontology.
tool_document_engineering: Survey reviews the evolution of tool use (ReAct-style calling -> Tool-Integrated Reasoning -> multi-turn TIR) and RL for tool selection/invocation, but does not prescribe a single tool-document/index engineering recipe. [uncertain]
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Survey discusses tool ecosystems and function-calling/TIR pipelines and AppWorld-style API environments (457 invokable APIs), and touches dynamic tool use; MCP/live-tool-store sync is not a dedicated analyzed axis. [uncertain]
tool_dependency_awareness: Not a dedicated analyzed axis; multi-tool/multi-API planning is acknowledged (e.g. AppWorld code-writing over many APIs) but inter-tool dependency modeling is not formalized. [uncertain]
adaptation_mechanism: N/A as a single mechanism (survey). Reviews adaptation via RL fine-tuning of the agentic policy (RLVR/PPO/GRPO), self-improvement/reflection, and RL-controlled memory update; no single CBR-style case-adaptation mechanism.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (survey, not a benchmark). It catalogs environments/benchmarks (Table 10) and frameworks (Table 11) with their domains/modalities/resource links rather than constructing a dataset.
